topic: Law change: PUC (Pollution Under Control) certificate validity now depends on emission norm, vehicle age and private/transport use - Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026 amending Rule 115(7), CMVR 1989, in force on Gazette publication (reported 19 Nov 2026); BS-I/II/III 3 months; BS-IV 6 months; BS-VI private (non-transport) up to 6 years 3 years, 6-10 years 1 year, over 10 years 6 months; BS-VI transport up to 6 years 2 years, 6-10 years 1 year, over 10 years 6 months; age from date of first registration; renewal within 10 days before expiry runs from old expiry date, late renewal runs afresh; existing certificates move to new schedule at first renewal

slides.title: New rules for your **PUC certificate**
slides.subtitle: How long your pollution certificate stays valid now depends on your vehicle's **age** and **emission norm**.
slides.cite: **Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026** · Amends Rule 115(7), CMV Rules, 1989 · Ministry of Road Transport and Highways · In force on publication in the Gazette

slides.label: Newer BS-VI vehicles
slides.title: BS-VI vehicles: **longer validity**
bullets: **Private** BS-VI vehicle up to 6 years old: PUC valid for **3 years**.
**Transport** (commercial) BS-VI vehicle up to 6 years old: valid for **2 years**.
Over 6 and up to 10 years: **1 year**. Over 10 years: **6 months**. This applies to both private and transport BS-VI vehicles.
slides.note: **Law fact:** A vehicle's age is counted from the date of its **first registration**.

slides.label: Older vehicles
slides.title: Older norms: **shorter validity**
bullets: **BS-I, BS-II and BS-III** vehicles: valid for only **3 months**.
Earlier, validity was set mainly by the **BS category**. Now the vehicle's **age** and its **private or commercial** use also count.

slides.label: Before you renew
slides.title: Renewing? **Keep these in mind**
bullets: Renew within the **10 days before expiry** and the new certificate starts from the old expiry date, so you lose nothing.
Renew **after expiry** and the new validity counts from the date of renewal, not from the old expiry date.
Your **current certificate stays valid** till it expires. The new periods apply from your first renewal after the change.

slides.label: Good to know
slides.title: Not every vehicle gets **3 years**
bullets: The 3-year period is only for **private BS-VI** vehicles up to **6 years** old.
Checks continue: in Delhi alone, **25,610 challans** were issued for not having a valid PUC between 1 and 17 November.
Check your vehicle's **emission norm** and **date of first registration** before your next renewal.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Your car's pollution certificate may now last up to 3 years 🚗🌿

The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has notified the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, which change Rule 115(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. The rules came into force on publication in the Official Gazette. How long a PUC (Pollution Under Control) certificate stays valid now depends on three things: the vehicle's emission norm, its age from the date of first registration, and whether it is a private or transport vehicle.

For BS-VI vehicles up to 6 years old, the PUC is valid for 3 years if the vehicle is private and 2 years if it is a transport vehicle. From over 6 up to 10 years, it is valid for 1 year, and after 10 years, only 6 months. BS-IV vehicles get 6 months, and BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles get just 3 months.

If you renew within the 10 days before your certificate expires, the new one starts from the old expiry date. If you renew late, the new validity counts from the renewal date. Your existing certificate stays valid until it expires; the new periods apply from your first renewal after the change.

Source: Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, amending Rule 115(7), Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (reported 19 November 2026)
